results.title: Europe’s China Auto Deal | Council on Foreign Relations
results.snippet:
China appears to have concluded that it prefers a guaranteed market for a limited number of cars (and more or less guaranteed profits) to the risk of a prohibitive tariff that would cut off all its exports.

And Europe preferred a negotiated deal to the risk of retaliation and a slowdown in licensing rare earth and magnet exports.

results.title: Rare Earth Magnet Costs Are Missing From Annual Reports | E+E Leader
results.snippet: Dysprosium, a rare earth metal that keeps the magnets in motors and generators working at high heat, now costs many times more outside China than inside it, yet the annual reports of manufacturers that depend on it describe the exposure without a single number.
